title: Super fund giant splashes $882m on Westfield Garden City
full_text:
Australian Retirement Trust (ART) has entered into an agreement to buy a 50 per cent interest in one of Australia’s largest shopping centres.
The super fund giant will pay $882.5m for a half share in Westfield Mount Gravatt - also known as Garden City - from ASX-listed Scentre Group subject to Australian Competition & Consumer Competition clearance.
If approved the sale is the largest single-asset retail transaction completed in Australia this calendar year, and follows ART’s record $3bn in Australian property investments in FY26.
The investment in Westfield Mt Gravatt follows ART’s $864m acquisition of a 19.9 per cent interest in Westfield Sydney in February
ART’s general manager Mid Risk Assets, Michael Weaver, said Westfield Mt Gravatt attracted millions of shoppers and offered development potential.
“At ART, we believe there is opportunity in the retail property market in Australia to generate strong long-term returns for members, especially for major assets that have demonstrated resilience,” he said.
The Brisbane headquartered company is one of Australia’s largest superannuation funds, managing more than $375bn in members’ retirement savings.
Scentre Group will continue to manage the major suburban retail centre following the completion of the acquisition.
Scentre Group chief executive Elliott Rusanow Westfield Mount Gravatt was one of the most popular centres in south-east Queensland, visited by more than 17 million customers last year and generating total business partner sales in excess of $1bn.
“Introducing new capital, through joint venturing our assets, forms a key part of our long-term strategic plan. In the last 13 months, we have announced approximately $3.1bn of new third party capital coming into the Group through the joint venturing of our assets,” he said.
“Today’s announcement continues to demonstrate our ability to source capital to pursue the Group’s strategic objectives of creating long term value for securityholders.”
ART’s long-term investment partner QIC will manage the super fund’s interest in the asset.
QIC Real Estate managing director Deborah Coakley said the transaction represented another important step in helping ART build a portfolio of Australia’s highest-quality retail assets. “The addition of Westfield Mt Gravatt complements ART’s investment in Westfield Sydney and reflects a disciplined approach to investing in assets with proven performance, strategic locations and long-term growth potential, while further strengthening the partnership between ART, QIC and Scentre Group.” she said.
Westfield Mount Gravatt is among Queensland’s biggest retail precincts, totalling 141,700 sqm with 376 tenants.
